chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sandal, from Kathir ibn Kathira, from Farwa ibn al-Ajuri, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites Surah Hud every Friday, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will raise him on the Day of Judgment in the company of the prophets, and no sin he committed will be known against him on the Day of Judgment.

key_terms.سُورَهَ هُودٍ: Surah Hud (the 11th chapter of the Quran)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Hud every Friday?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual elevation gained by regularly reciting Surah Hud on Fridays, linking the surah’s themes of prophetic patience and divine justice to the reward of resurrection among the prophets. The promise that the reciter’s sins will not be 'known' or held against them reflects the Shia concept of divine mercy overriding minor faults for those who maintain consistent devotion. This practice underscores the Friday ritual's role in spiritual purification and alignment with the prophetic legacy.
